metadata.title: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [August 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.43

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [August 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.43
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.43
- Datum: 08.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
By Clipper and by steamer

Dear Hanna and Manfred,
Finally I have settled Eva and I hope she
will be happy there, they are nice welltodo Americans, the man in
the smeltering business, kind-hearted, extremely fond of children,
jolly, their house in a very good neighbourhood in the suburbs of
Newyork - forty minutes by car - already countryside, near a lake.
I have not been out there myself as I spoke to Mr. Salmon only
yesterday and the wife is coming to Newyork to meet me - so I could
not insist on going out there especially as our time is now over-
crowded these last two days. But I am absolutely sure that there
is nothing to worry about the house and the surroundings. Rose
who brought me together with him told me that it is a very good
naighbourhood with excellent schoold and from what he told me it
is a very nice and large house and she will be looked after per-
fectly well. As they are definitely wealthy people there is nothing
to worry about from the financial point of view, he is eager to have
a child, to look after her, and what he would like best is to keep
her and marry her one day. He and his wife are college graduates,
she is, as he says "an artist", I believe she paints. He will see
that she continues her piano lessons, told me that there are plenty
of children in the neighbourhood, amongst them a thirteen year old
boy, a definite genius on the piano, and she will meet
nice children there. They are not too intellectual, but are having
a very good time, helping when they can, but enjoying life, and I
believe Eva will be in a pleasant and carefree atmosphere and feel
happy there. In any case Rose Wohl will go and visit her and let
me know how she is feeling there, and Rose also promised me to find
another home should this one not turn out as well as we expect. I
wish I could have stayed until Eva arrives, bring her to her new
home and see myself how she feels - but we have to leave, our time
is up and you know that we are expected to go to South America.
What you have to do now - if you have not
done so yet - is to cable Mr. Leon S. Salmon, 291 Beechmont Drive,
New Rochelle, New York, when Eva is arriving, so that he can fetch
her from the boat. He is very impatient to have her here, and I
hope you have not to wait too long for a boat and that she gets here
safely. Did you try the Palestine Orient Lloyd for a ticket? You know
we got ours there. -
I would also recommend that you cable also
Dr. Viola Wertheim Bernard (who was only the person to send the
affidavit as a special favour but who, I expect, will not take any
special interest in Eva) about Eva's arrival and where she is going
to live so that she is informed. I shall write her in any case and
tell her about it before I leave, but it is better that she knows
when Eva is coming and that she also informs the United States
Committee for European Children (215 Fourth Avenue) who want to
check up all the children whose affidavits went through their office
as Evas did.
I hope that Eva will not feel too lonely
arriving in a foreign country and being met by strange people, but
it cannot be helped. Rose might go down too to fetch her, but she
does not know her either.
pages.notes: Typoskript. Am linken Rand handschriftliche Notiz von Stefan Zweig: 'In any case Rose Wohl, 258 east 7th Street, Newyork, 18 West 70th Street Newyork. 175 East 79th Street Newyork. You probably won't want my notes in law address, but here it is to: Stefanie Zweig, 18 West 70th Street Newyork.' Am oberen Rand handschriftliche Notiz: 'and most people of our sort, We will try our best for Heiner, but the time is now short'.

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah, for Eva all is now well prepared as you
have heard by our cable - they are wealthy people in a
large house in an elegant faubourg of Newyork and they
are really eager to have a good educated child. We see them
today for lunch. All was more difficult than we expected
as everybody is away from Newyork and this is also the major
difficulty for the affidavit for Heiner - I cannot ask one
from Heubal as he has given already too many and I do not
know if we can find anybody in these last two overcrowded
days. Till now I could not have any[?] definitive for my
former wife, I am trying now to get Mexican visas for
her whole family.
Thousand thanks that you have settled all about the
house in Bath, I hope you will have there sometimes a
good rest after the busy days in London.
We had here a hard time, as I have worked a good deal
merely small things, but we will have rest during the twelve
days on the ship. I have offers for lectures in Argentine
Uruguay, Chile, Venezuela, more than I will probably
do and you must not worry about us. Dont be too
economical and send us cables to Rio (from where we
send immediately our Hoteladress) - I do not
rely on airmail. In great love and hurry your
We arrive in Rio the 21. August                                Stefan
pages.notes: Handschrift in violetter Tinte. 'Heiner' ist über 'things' eingefügt. 'during' ist über 'rest' eingefügt.
Farbskala/Grauskala fuer Archivierung. Überdeckt den Text von Seite 2.
